The note from the tribe had been urgent, speaking of a creature with incredible strength and even greater brutality having claimed several lives and injuring over a dozen guards during its capture. Thad'ja Songcatcher had left without haste and though he had taken the fastest transport available it had still taken him several days to arrive. 5 days had passed since the creatures attack, 3 since the letter had arrived at the great tree but at last the shaman had arrived before the gates to the Grove of Hom. Passing through the gates under cover of darkness the Shaman was quickly escorted to a large tent that had been erected in the market square to conceal the creature and its' cage from from view as it had apparently been corraled into a recently aquired sentinel that was due to be erected as a monument. "Good evening Shaman" spoke a voice as the Shaman entered the tent, standing before him was Ma'te, one of the twin Chieftains of the tribe and behind him his sister Lo'te, partner to the throne and the remaining members of the council of Elders "I came as quickly as I could" the Shaman replied, greeting the council with a bow "Now please if you would, tell me what you can of this creature, i have many questions" "It is a foul beast" The Chieftain spat turning to face the spherical prison "It dares to wear the skin of our kin while it feeds upon their flesh" A rustling came from within the sphere in response to the Chieftains words "I understand you had difficulty containing it" "Yes... it took 12 of our best men and women and the destruction of two of our brewing vats to contain it, the injuries were.... significant. "I'll need to see the creature" the Shaman replied, approaching the sentinel with caution "Did you not just hear what I said?!" exclaimed the Chieftain incredulously "It took a small army and the luck of the Gods themselves to capture it, I would not dare risk its release" "Nevertheless I must see the beast if we are to learn anything of its origin, otherwise my presence here is pointless" "Very well" the Chieftain replied, shaking his head "But I will not have another one of my kin injured by that beast, I will send for the Cuirass." After the Cuirass of Hom was delivered to the tribe by the God of Agriculture himself, the Elder council had it sealed away until such time that it was needed for the tribe revered its power so much that they would not call upon it unless left with no other option. Within moments of the council's instruction two guards appeared carrying an ornate chest between them. Within the chest lay a cuirass of verdant green inscribed with runes of great power, granting the user control over a portion of the great vines of Hom. After securing the cuirass to their Chieftain the guards exited the tent leaving the Council and the Shaman alone with the creature once more. "At your word Shaman" The Chieftain said, his words tained with his objection "very well then, release it"
